newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to protest to Turkey over Istanbul blast.
newsitem.headline: Greece to protest to Turkey over Istanbul blast.

text.p: Greece said on Monday it would protest to Turkey over a grenade attack against the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate in Istanbul by urban Islamic guerrillas.

A government spokesman said the Patriarchate building, the seat of Orthodox Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomeos I, who is the spiritual head of 250 million Orthodox Christians worldwide, should have been better guarded.
"We protest against this action and we will ask for a full investigation in order to shed light on how this incident happened," spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.

Earlier on Monday the armed Islamist group Great Eastern Islamic Raiders - Front (IBDA-C) said it was responsible for throwing the grenade in the Patriarchate garden. The blast caused damage but there were no casualties.
Four suspected members of the group were arrested in late 1994 for allegedly attacking the Patriarchate earlier that year.

"The Greek government will undertake all diplomatic action to express its displeasure and to ask the Turkish government to condemn the incident...which undermine conditions for communication between the two countries," Reppas said.
NATO members Greece and neighbouring Turkey are at odds over a number of issues, including the dwindling Greek community in Istanbul, rights in the Aegean Sea and the divided island of Cyprus.
